Thank you for leading this project on your side. The onboarding went smoothly mostly because of how well prepared your team was.

Best regards

notes.subject: Loss review notes
notes.body:
Loss review call with {first_name}, about 30 minutes. They told us last week that they chose another vendor. I asked for this call to understand why, and {first_name} was generous with their time.

Their decision, in their words: "Your product was better at what it does, but the other one does more things, and we needed to reduce the number of tools."

Details:
- The winning vendor offers call recording, transcription, forecasting and summaries in one platform.
- Their summaries are less reliable, in {first_name}'s opinion, but the CFO preferred one contract over three.
- Price was not the main reason. The total cost of the other platform was actually higher, but it replaced three existing tools.

What we did well, according to {first_name}:
- The demo with their own data was the strongest of all vendors.
- Citations and the "not enough information" behavior were mentioned positively by everyone.
- The pilot was well organized and the weekly reports were useful.

What we could have done better:
- We focused too much on the sales team and didn't engage the CFO early. By the time the CFO got involved, the decision framework was "fewest tools", not "best results".
- Our proposal arrived about a week later than the competitor's.
- We didn't have a clear answer to "what tool does this replace".
- Generation time during the live demo created a bad first impression with one executive, even though it didn't matter in the pilot.

Things {first_name} said might change:
- If the other platform's summaries cause problems, they might come back. {first_name} said the sales director is already skeptical.
- Their contract with the other vendor is 1 year, so the next decision point is in about 11 months.

Lessons for us:
1. Identify the economic buyer early and understand their decision criteria.
2. Prepare a "what does this replace" answer before the proposal stage.
3. Never generate briefs live in executive demos, use pre-generated ones.
4. Send proposals within 3 business days.

Next steps:
- Send a thank you note.
- Set a reminder 9 months from now to check in before their renewal.
- Share these lessons with the sales team in our next meeting.

notes.subject: Thanks for the honest feedback
notes.body:
Hi {first_name},

Thank you for taking the time to walk me through your decision yesterday. It's not common for someone to be that open after choosing another vendor, and I really appreciate it.

I wanted to summarize what I heard, so you can correct me if I misunderstood anything:

- The main reason was consolidation. Your leadership wanted fewer tools, and the other platform covers recording, transcription, forecasting and summaries in one contract.
- Our product was seen as stronger on accuracy and trust, especially the citations and the way it says when there isn't enough information.
- The timing of our proposal and the lack of a clear answer on which tool we'd replace hurt us.
- The executive who saw the live demo was put off by the waiting time.

These are fair points, and we're taking them seriously. We've already changed how we run demos for executives, and we're working on a clearer story about where we fit next to platforms like the one you chose.

I'd like to stay in touch, with no pressure. If the new platform covers everything you need, that's a good outcome for your team. If at some point the summaries cause problems, or your needs change, I'd be glad to talk again. I'll reach out briefly before your renewal next year, unless you tell me otherwise.

Also, if it's useful, I'm happy to share our notes from the pilot, including the questions your reps asked most often. They might help you configure the new tool.

Thanks again, and good luck with the rollout.

Best regards

notes.subject: Re-engagement call after a year
notes.body:
Call with {first_name}, about 35 minutes. We last spoke about a year ago, when they chose another vendor. They reached out this time, which is a good sign.

What happened in the last year at {company}:
- They rolled out the all in one platform they chose last year.
- Recording and transcription work fine.
- Summaries have been a problem. {first_name} gave two examples: one summary said a customer had agreed to a price that was never agreed, and another attributed a quote to the wrong person. In the first case, a rep repeated the wrong price to the customer, which was embarrassing.
- After that, the sales director told reps not to trust the summaries without checking the recording, which defeats the purpose.

Changes on their side:
- The CFO who pushed for consolidation left the company.
- The new CFO is more open to specialized tools if they show clear value.
- The sales team grew from 25 to 40 people.
- They opened a new team in Colombia, with notes mostly in Spanish.

What {first_name} wants now:
- Reliable summaries with sources, which they remember as our strength.
- Something that works with notes and transcripts from the platform they already have.
- A solution for the Spanish speaking team.

What I shared:
- We now support importing transcripts from their current platform through its export.
- Briefs are pre-generated and faster than when they saw the demo.
- Spanish notes work well for summaries, question answering is still improving.
- Our evaluation results, including citation validity and tests for unsupported claims.

Concerns from {first_name}:
- They can't cancel the current platform, since recording and transcription work well. So we'd be an add on, and the price has to make sense next to it.
- The sales director will want a short pilot to compare summaries side by side.

Next steps:
- Send a short note on how we'd integrate with their current platform.
- Propose a 4 week side by side comparison with 10 reps, including 3 from the Colombia team.
- {first_name} will talk to the new CFO about budget for the next quarter.

My assessment: real opportunity this time. The pain is concrete, the old blocker is gone, and we already have trust with {first_name}.

notes.subject: Catching up after your reorganization
notes.body:
Hi {first_name},

I hope things have settled down after the reorganization. It's been a few months since we last spoke, and I didn't want to reach out too early while everything was changing.

I've been thinking about our conversations from last year. At the time, your main concerns were the handoffs between account owners and the time reps spent preparing for calls. With the new combined team, I imagine those challenges might be even bigger, since reps now cover accounts they didn't know before.

A few things have changed on our side since we last talked, in case they're relevant:

- Briefs can now be prepared automatically before meetings on reps' calendars, so there's no waiting time.
- Reps can ask questions like "what did they object to last time" or "who else is involved in the decision" and get answers with links to the original notes.
- When there isn't enough information about a contact, the brief says so clearly instead of filling the gap.
- We can import historical notes from CSV, with duplicate detection by email, which might help if the two teams' CRMs are being merged.

I'm not assuming any of this is a priority right now. If it is, I'd be happy to do a short session for you and the new head of the combined unit, using a few of your real accounts. If it's not, I'd be grateful if you could tell me roughly when it might make sense to reconnect, so I don't bother you before then.

Either way, congratulations on getting through what sounded like a very demanding period.

Best regards
